solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vessel with last of Medoc put before shrine

indicators.note: put before says the Medoc letter goes in front of the shrine word
last of points to the final letter of the wine name Medoc

parts.note: an oracle is a shrine where a god was consulted

explanation.surface: A wine-themed offering: a bottle of Medoc set out in front of a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Dull king features in class teacher prepared

indicators.note: features in says the king's letter appears inside the rearranged letters
prepared means made ready, so the letters of class teacher are worked into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A class teacher prepares a dull lesson that features a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Characterless means lacking distinctive qualities, which is to say dull.

clue.text: Chafing from sound defeat after loss of crown

indicators.note: the crown of a down word is its top, so the defeat word loses its first letter

parts.note: a drubbing is a sound, thorough defeat

explanation.surface: A monarch smarts from a heavy defeat that cost the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing and chafing both mean friction wearing against the skin.

clue.text: Rodent evasive climbing out of bed

parts.note: coy means evasive, reluctant to give details

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: up means out of bed

explanation.surface: A shy rodent creeps out of its bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns UP into PU in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent, also called the nutria.

clue.text: Stretch note (eg "la") with vibrato perhaps

indicators.note: vibrato wobbles a sung note, so the letters of note, eg and la are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A singing tip: hold a note such as la, adding vibrato.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen, to stretch out.

clue.text: Majority of cattle docked both times in city

indicators.note: docked means cut short at the tail, so the majority word loses its last letter

parts.note: most means the majority

indicators.note: both times says the docking applies again, so the cattle word also loses its last letter

parts.note: cows are cattle

explanation.surface: A farming report: most of the herd had their tails docked, twice over, in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked both times' clips MOST to MOS and COWS to COW.
explanation.definitionFit: Moscow is the capital city of Russia.

clue.text: Second person that's attractive and stylish

parts.note: mo is an informal word for a moment or second
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A runner-up who is good-looking and well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish means fashionable, in the current mode, so stylish.

clue.text: Grave a nun tries to vandalise

indicators.note: to vandalise is to smash up, so the letters of a nun tries are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun attempts to deface a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective, solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy and solemn in temper, as grave does.

clue.text: In theory, sole recipe needs mash as a filling

indicators.note: as a filling says the mash word is stuffed inside the other pieces

parts.note: sole means one, only
pap is soft mushy food, a mash
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe for sole that calls for a mashed stuffing, at least in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like the fish but means one.
explanation.definitionFit: On paper is an idiom for in theory, as opposed to in practice.

clue.text: Record of blue jays regularly stopping overseas?

indicators.note: stopping says the picked letters plug a gap inside the overseas word

parts.note: abroad means overseas

indicators.note: regularly says to take letters at a steady interval through blue jays, here every third

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's log of blue jays seen at intervals while travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every third letter of 'blue jays', B, E, Y, which go inside ABROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbey Road is the famous Beatles album, a record in the music sense.

clue.text: Stone to shoot when whirled

indicators.note: whirled means spun round, so the word for shoot is turned to face backwards

parts.note: to zap is to shoot

explanation.surface: A sling: a stone to fire off once it has been spun around.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a gemstone, so a stone in the jeweller's sense.

clue.text: The Stripes supporting the 4 on 8?

parts.note: the Beatles, the famous four, walked across a striped road crossing on the cover of the album named at 8 across

explanation.surface: A band called the Stripes backs a famous foursome on another record.
explanation.walkthrough: The four are the Beatles, photographed walking over the black-and-white stripes on the 8 across cover; a zebra crossing is the British name for a striped pedestrian crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abbey Road cover shows the Beatles on a pedestrian crossing painted in stripes.

clue.text: Defrocked women united after so long

indicators.note: defrocked means stripped of the outer garment, so the women word loses its outside letters

parts.note: ladies are women
U is the standard abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Women stripped of their religious orders band together after a long service.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell, the French goodbye, as is the informal so long.

clue.text: A grub stop possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of a grub stop could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A place to stop for grub, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub serving good food, literally a place to stop for grub.

clue.text: Leaders of ships in Bath eating good porridge

indicators.note: eating says the bath word takes the abbreviation for good inside it

parts.note: a tub is a bath
porridge is made of oats

explanation.surface: Ship captains in the city of Bath tuck into a bowl of porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the English city but is just a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Tugboats tow and guide larger vessels into harbour, leading the ships.

clue.text: Blanks 007 essentially needed on jobs

parts.note: the essential, middle character of 007 is a zero, read as the letter O
missions are jobs or assignments, like those of a secret agent

explanation.surface: James Bond is on assignments that draw a blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle character of 007 is a zero, read as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Omissions are gaps, things left out, which is what blanks are.

clue.text: Rear is shot in range

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of rear is fall apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone on a shooting range takes a bullet in the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a mountain range, the Spanish word as in Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Simple sleuth's witticism lecturer ignored

indicators.note: ignored says the lecturer's letter is left out of the sleuth's name

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes is the archetypal sleuth
a pun is a witticism

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes makes a plain joke that a lecturer pays no heed to.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, so simple.

clue.text: Stagger back on pass crossing Italy

parts.note: re means on, concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: crossing says the pass word straddles the letter for Italy

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A walker reels back in shock while crossing an Alpine pass into Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to spring or flinch backwards, as to stagger back does.

clue.text: Squiggle under letter from detective in first cell?

indicators.note: in says the detective's abbreviation is placed within the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
DI is a detective inspector
A is a first, the top grade

explanation.surface: A detective's letter scrawled from inside a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the hook mark written below a c, as in façade.

clue.text: Relative who's passed Spooner's pig market

indicators.note: Spooner's says to swap the opening sounds of the two words, as the Reverend Spooner did by accident

parts.note: a boar is a male pig
a fair is a market

explanation.surface: Grandad, now dead, once ran the local pig market.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BOAR FAIR gives FORE BEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is an ancestor, a relative from an earlier generation now dead.

clue.text: Award hanging from nobleman's dangly bit

indicators.note: hanging from says in this down light the award comes below the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A medal dangling from an aristocrat's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The earlobe is the soft hanging part at the bottom of the ear.

clue.text: Sluggish swim over at foot of hill

indicators.note: at foot of says the swim word sits below the hill word in this down light

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: over says the swim word is turned round

parts.note: a dip is a swim

explanation.surface: A sluggish swimmer finishes at the bottom of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpid means lethargic and inactive, so sluggish.

clue.text: Probing camera with exposed lens bashes bear

indicators.note: exposed means with the outer cover taken off, so lens keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: dos are parties, informally bashes
to cope with something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A photographer's lens left uncapped gets smashed by a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips LENS to EN; 'bashes' is the noun, parties, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An endoscope is a medical camera on a tube used to look inside the body.

clue.text: Source of infection right inside bits of 9?

indicators.note: inside says the letter for right sits within the word for bits of the stone

parts.note: 9 across is a topaz, a gem, so precious pieces of that kind are gems

explanation.surface: Pieces of a gemstone turn out to be the source of an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Germs are microbes that spread disease, a source of infection.

clue.text: Celts trap the Spanish with chemical weapon

indicators.note: trap says the weapon word holds the Spanish article inside it

parts.note: gas is a chemical weapon
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Celtic warriors corner Spanish soldiers using poison gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaels are Gaelic-speaking people of Ireland and Scotland, Celts.

clue.text: Discharge some dress-rehearsal volunteers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Volunteers at a dress rehearsal are dismissed, or some of them are.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns.

clue.text: Topping peak, Edmund posed initially with lager

indicators.note: initially says to take the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: Peroni is an Italian brand of lager

explanation.surface: Edmund Hillary posing on the summit of Everest with a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage used as a pizza topping.

clue.text: Fallen part of church in centre of building

indicators.note: in says the church part sits between the two letters taken from building
centre of picks the two middle letters of building

parts.note: an apse is the rounded end part of a church

explanation.surface: Part of a church in the middle of a building has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' gives LD, the middle pair of 'building', which holds APSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsed means fallen away from a faith or practice, as in a lapsed Catholic.

clue.text: Savings invested by Pyongyang get sent back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
by here means held by, so the answer is carried within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Money invested in North Korea's capital gets sent home again.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no hiding signal: 'by' (held by) points into 'Pyongyang get sent', where GGETSEN read 'back' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money saved up for the future, savings put by.
